import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load_inline


# Define custom CUDA kernel for element-wise Tanh activation.
elementwise_tanh_source = """
#include <torch/extension.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>

__global__ void tanh_kernel(const float* input, float* output, int size) {
    int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (idx < size) {
        output[idx] = tanhf(input[idx]);
    }
}

torch::Tensor elementwise_tanh_cuda(torch::Tensor a) {
    auto size = a.numel();
    auto out = torch::zeros_like(a);

    const int block_size = 256;
    const int num_blocks = (size + block_size - 1) / block_size;

    tanh_kernel<<<num_blocks, block_size>>>(a.data_ptr<float>(), out.data_ptr<float>(), size);

    return out;
}
"""

# Compile the inline CUDA code for element-wise Tanh
elementwise_tanh = load_inline(
    name="elementwise_tanh",
    cpp_sources=("torch::Tensor elementwise_tanh_cuda(torch::Tensor a)();"),
    cuda_sources=elementwise_tanh_source,
    functions=["elementwise_tanh_cuda"],
    verbose=True,
    extra_cflags=[],
    extra_ldflags=[],
)


class ModelNew(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.tanh = elementwise_tanh

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Applies Tanh activation to the input tensor.

        Args:
            x (torch.Tensor): Input tensor of any shape.

        Returns:
            torch.Tensor: Output tensor with Tanh applied, same shape as input.
        """
        return self.tanh.elementwise_tanh_cuda(x)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Quick sanity check (not part of the required output)
    model = ModelNew()
    x = torch.rand(1, 393216).cuda()
    out = model(x)
    assert out.shape == x.shape
    print("ModelNew forward pass succeeded.")
